bull_bear.body:
- Dainik Jagran has remained the largest-read newspaper and has consistently maintained its market leadership position since 2003, giving strong brand popularity, extensive reach and rich content versus peers
- Deep regional connect and a strong on-ground network that generates a large volume of original, credible local content not readily available to others — including to global technology players
- Multi-platform ecosystem across print, radio, digital, OOH and activations that allows integrated, cross-media campaigns for advertisers
- Strong credit profile — ratings reaffirmed at AA+/Stable for long and medium-term instruments and A1+ for short-term; subsidiaries Music Broadcast (AA/Stable, A1+) and Midday Infomedia (AA(-)/Stable) also rated
- Digital properties continue to rank amongst the top 15 in the country in the news and information category (Comscore Mar'26)
- Ranked among India's top 10 OOH companies with media-owning leadership positions across multiple cities, and leadership in Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand covering 17 cities
- Radio City garnered an 18% market share in FY26
- Distribution and asset base of 32 printing facilities, 39 radio stations and 3,500+ OOH media assets
- Partnerships with Google, Meta, Jio and Amazon supporting content discovery, distribution and syndication
- Repeated year-after-year recognition by professional bodies for enterprise technology capability, supporting internal controls and process efficiency
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Unresolved promoter/promoter-group dispute before the NCLT, carried as an auditor Emphasis of Matter — The auditors draw attention to Note 24(v) describing a petition under Sections 241, 242 and 244 of the Companies Act, 2013 filed by certain promoters and promoter group members against other promoters and promoter group members, pending with the National Company Law Tribunal. The Company also filed an appeal with the NCLAT against its holding company Jagran Media Investment Network Private Limited's request to convene an EGM seeking shareholders' approval for removal of 7 independent directors and 1 whole-time director; the NCLAT permitted the EGM to be held on May 29, 2026 by its order dated May 26, 2026 but directed that implementation of the proposed resolution be kept in abeyance until the outcome of the NCLT petition. Board composition and effective control of the Company therefore remain contested, although management currently does not expect any impact of the matter.
- Circulation remains below pre-Covid levels, capping advertisement revenue growth — Circulation declined substantially after the Covid-19 pandemic and continues to remain below pre-Covid levels, which management states 'does not augur well for achieving significant growth in advertisement revenues'. Cover-price increases taken to offset newsprint costs led to a sharper-than-expected decline in circulation across publishers, and changing reading habits, particularly in larger cities, have compounded it. Because advertisement pricing follows circulation and readership, a structurally lower circulation base constrains the largest revenue line.
- Newsprint price volatility on the primary raw material — Newsprint, the primary raw material, constitutes a significant portion of overall expenses and any material increase adversely impacts profitability in a significant manner. Prices had softened substantially to USD 500-550 per tonne from a peak of nearly USD 1,000 per tonne witnessed a few years ago, but recent supply-chain disruptions from geopolitical conflict in the Persian Gulf region have again driven a considerable increase. The exposure hits both cost and revenue, because elevated newsprint also causes the company to hold back circulation expansion.
- Structural disruption of digital audience and monetisation by AI search and global platform gatekeepers — Management flags a decline in unique visitors in the news and information category over the previous year, attributed to AI-led search, META's reduced focus on news content, changes in Google's algorithms and cookie deprecation. The Group also faces intense competition for digital revenues from domestic and global technology giants such as Google and Facebook, which command a dominant share of the digital advertising market, and is significantly dependent on advertisement revenues generated through networks owned by those same platforms. Management states this dependence, coupled with an inability to effectively monetise content, may render the business model unsustainable over the long term, and that content monetisation remains a challenge so profitable growth may take longer than originally envisaged.
- Highly fragmented, intensely competitive print market plus cross-media substitution — India's print media market is highly fragmented, with intense competition posing challenges to the profit-earning capacity of print companies, while other media platforms, particularly digital media, continue to pose a competitive threat. Management's offsetting argument rests on print's inherent advantages of credibility, localised content and affordable accessibility, on the reinforcing effect of fake news circulating elsewhere, and on Dainik Jagran having remained the largest-read newspaper with market leadership consistently maintained since 2003.
- Single-reportable-segment and advertisement-revenue concentration — The Company reports no reportable segment other than print under IndAS-108 'Operating Segment Reporting'. Advertisement revenue accounted for 75.3% of total print and digital revenue (previous year 74.2%) against circulation at 22.4% (previous year 23.6%), and advertisement revenue grew 4.2% while circulation revenue de-grew 2.4%. With earnings so heavily geared to a single medium and a single advertising cycle, there is little internal offset when ad spend or newsprint turns against the company.
- Climate change, water security and supply-chain transition risk on a paper-and-ink input base — The BRSR material-issues table identifies Climate Change and Resilience as both risk and opportunity, noting that operations can be directly affected by critical sustainability risks including climate change, water security, plastic waste, supply chain disruptions and sourcing challenges, alongside regulatory and market transition risks associated with the shift to a low-carbon economy — changing consumer preferences, increased product costs, and future government policies and regulations. The company's primary consumption is large quantities of printing inks and paper. Stated financial implication is negative in the short to medium term (mitigation costs) and positive in the long term.
- Dependence on key executive talent in a competitive market for skilled professionals — The BRSR material-issues table records that the success of the Company's operations relies on the ongoing dedication, skills and expertise of its corporate and divisional executive teams, as well as other highly qualified employees with extensive knowledge in business, technology and operations. Because the business is a people-and-content business with no capacity moat, loss of senior editorial, commercial or technology talent translates directly into competitive position.

business.body: Jagran Prakashan publishes newspapers and magazines in Hindi, Punjabi and Urdu, led by Dainik Jagran, and monetises that audience primarily through the sale of advertisement space and newspaper circulation. Around the print core it runs four adjacent media verticals — radio (Radio City, through subsidiary Music Broadcast Limited), digital news and information portals, out-of-home media (hoardings, billboards, transit and retail branding) and on-ground brand activations and events. Its customers are both institutional advertisers (corporates, agencies, government departments, educational institutions and NGOs) and individual readers and listeners across metros and emerging regional markets in India.

- **Radio:** Radio City
- **Digital:** 19 digital media portals across news, health, women, education, entertainment and fact-checking
- **Out-of-home:** Hoardings and billboards, Metro media and station branding, Transit media including bus shelters, metro stations and railway stations, Retail branding, including in-shop and out-shop media, Digital formats including LED and smart displays
- **Activation:** Brand activations and experiential campaigns, Event management and corporate engagements, Rural marketing, conferences and exhibitions, Shopper and retail marketing, Public health and social awareness programmes, Creative strategy and content development, Integrated media campaigns

outlook.body:
- Run an integrated multi-platform ecosystem — print, radio, digital, out-of-home and activations — so that content, audiences, technology and engagement combine into unified, high-impact campaigns for advertisers as the boundaries between media segments blur.
- Defend and extend the print core through trust, unmatched reach and deep regional influence, while deploying targeted forward-looking initiatives to strengthen circulation and reader engagement whose benefits are expected to become increasingly visible over time.
- Manage newsprint cost exposure through a four-fold approach: raising cover prices, optimising the newsprint mix, cutting consumption via pages-per-copy optimisation, and avoiding circulation expansion into areas not relevant to advertisers.
- Structurally recalibrate the radio business — restructuring and cost optimisation combined with a diversified revenue mix built on high-margin digital initiatives, sponsorships, special events and client-centric solutions.
- Accelerate investment in digital platforms, content capabilities and audience engagement to expand presence across next-generation media formats, with content, data and technology at the core of the strategy.
- Diversify digital beyond news into health, women, education, entertainment and fact-checking across all three formats — text, audio and video — and monetise content, including bringing some offerings under subscription models.
- Leverage partnerships with Google, Meta, Jio and Amazon to strengthen content discovery, distribution and syndication, and use the reach of social media personalities including those from its own newsrooms.
- Shift the outdoor business towards asset-led operations and pursue premium inventory, digital innovation and technology-led applications; in activations, pivot to high-margin, scalable and value-accretive engagements.
- Maintain disciplined cost management and operational prudence — rationalising and cutting expenses where circumstances warrant, while taking care that long-term business interest is not compromised.
- Improve return on capital via a two-fold strategy: continually improve profits and return on assets, and return surplus cash to shareholders without compromising business needs.
- Embed sustainability and governance into value creation — responsible resource use, energy conservation and waste management on the environmental side, and the flagship 'Saat Sarokaar' community programme spanning education, healthcare, women empowerment, environmental sustainability, water conservation, poverty alleviation and population awareness.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Jagran Prakashan's FY26 expansion as described in this bundle is platform- and product-led rather than plant-led: no new printing facility, radio station or physical site addition is announced, and no rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in the routed text. The existing footprint is given as counts rather than capacity — 39 radio stations, 3,500+ out-of-home media inventory and 7 cities of presence, with print and radio spanning 13 states and union territories in addition to 39 key radio markets. The build-out that is actually described is digital. Jagran New Media deployed a 'Newsroom 2.0' framework for real-time, insight-led, multi-format storytelling and introduced an AI-powered smart CMS to improve content creation, distribution efficiency and packaging at scale, alongside a Single Sign-On (SSO) framework to enable seamless access, improved journey mapping and personalised engagement; platforms are stated to be compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA). Product and regional expansion in FY26 comprised the launch of the Gujarati Jagran App and the transformation of the English news platform into a standalone premium destination, TheDailyJagran.com, with a refreshed brand identity; JNM publishes across 12 languages including Marathi, Gujarati, Tamil and Punjabi, and expanded hyperlocal coverage and editorial-led video programming. Alongside the platform work, the company says it continued to diversify and scale alternate revenue streams through focused expansion across events, IPs, production capabilities, content-to-commerce initiatives and subscription-led models, plus content-led commerce, premium content models, branded storytelling, syndication and licensing partnerships and video/OTT monetisation. In out-of-home the stated expansion is a higher contribution from asset-based formats and stronger execution capabilities rather than new inventory build, and in activations it is a rationalised portfolio prioritising scalable and value-accretive engagements. No rupee capex figure is available: the Capital Commitments and Segment Capital Expenditure named-disclosure blocks supplied with this bundle carry only heading lines and no attributable figures.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management believes circulation has stabilised after the decline since the onset of the pandemic in 2020, and expects to achieve the desired circulation growth in the current year on the back of various initiatives.
- Reasonable newsprint prices provide adequate scope to focus on increasing circulation; the current price hike caused by Persian Gulf geopolitical conflict is expected to be temporary, with prices likely to stabilise at reasonable levels once the conflict subsides.
- Newsprint had softened to USD 500-550 per tonne from a peak of nearly USD 1,000 per tonne a few years ago before the recent supply-chain-driven escalation; a return to reasonable levels should help maintain stability in performance.
- Per capita spending on media consumption in India remains significantly lower than global standards, so management believes all media platforms have potential to grow, though growth rates will vary by penetration and maturity of each platform — 'no medium is redundant'.
- Print's inherent advantages — credibility, localised content, and easy and affordable accessibility — are reinforced by the increasing circulation of fake news across other platforms.
- Government-led digital impetus is driving higher growth across tier-I and tier-II towns and rural India, giving the Group an edge and making its digital offering more relevant to consumers and to global platforms such as Google that procure content from publishers.
- Global technology players are gradually recognising the value of content generated by the print industry and becoming more willing to pay for it, supporting the Group's original local-content advantage.
- Digital content monetisation remains a challenge, and accordingly profitable growth in digital may take longer than originally envisaged.
- Media and entertainment is being reshaped by evolving consumer preferences, rapid digital adoption, technological advancement and growing demand for personalised and regional content, with advertisers increasingly seeking integrated solutions combining reach, engagement and measurable outcomes.
- Digital media remains the primary growth engine of the sector, propelled by mobile consumption, video, social platforms, creator ecosystems and data-driven advertising; out-of-home capitalises on rapid urbanisation, infrastructure development and digital formats; experiential activations enable deeper immersive brand connections.
- Advertising demand in FY26 was subdued across certain sectors and the print business also had to navigate a higher base; radio revenue was impacted by a challenging advertising environment.
- Radio restructuring and cost optimisation measures implemented during the year yielded a return to positive operating profitability in the final quarter of FY26.
- Outdoor and activation momentum was catalysed by a strategic shift towards asset-led outdoor operations and growing demand for experiential brand engagement; management is confident this segment is well-positioned to generate significant long-term value.
- Standalone operating profit margin improvement was attributed to higher advertisement revenue, cost optimisation with strict budgetary control, and higher operating profit at Naidunia and the outdoor business.
- Depreciation is provided largely on the written down value method rather than the straight line method used by peers, so the charge is significantly higher in initial years and declines over time, helping in difficult periods; there was no major capital expenditure incurred during the year.
- The Group ended FY26 with a strong consolidated net cash position of approximately ₹1,200 crore, providing financial strength and flexibility to support the long-term growth strategy.
- The Company has operated without a Managing Director since October 1, 2023 amid inter se disputes among Promoter/Promoter Group members; the outcome remains uncertain and the future course of action depends on resolution of the disputes and/or the final outcome of ongoing legal proceedings.
